about: Budgets for scripts/perf-measure.sh, compared by scripts/perf-budget.py in the Performance budget job (#853). Every metric is lower-is-better. baseline is the number a budget was set from; budget is the most a pull request may measure. Raising a budget is a reviewed change: say why in the pull request. Baselines are the median of eight merge queue runs on GitHub runners, 2026-10-20, both architectures (the perf-amd64 and perf-arm64 artifacts). Image sizes are deterministic (under 0.5 MB apart across those runs) and get 10%. Times and memory vary between runners, so their budgets sit at about 2.5 to 5 times the worst run seen (memory, which moved 17 MB across the runs, at 280). Delivery latency is measured at 1.5 requests a second for 60 seconds, about 30 samples per target, so its budget catches large regressions only. Sizes are MB, times seconds or milliseconds, memory is the API's resident MB after 60 s idle on 2 CPUs.
